# Didache Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_010_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 10

**1** When everyone has had enough to eat, pray this prayer of thanksgiving:

**2** Holy Father, we thank you — for your holy name, which has made its home in our hearts, and for the knowledge, faith, and immortality you revealed to us through your servant Jesus. Glory be to you forever.

**3** Lord of all, you created everything for the sake of your name. You gave food and drink to all people to enjoy — so that they would thank you. And to us, you gave something more: spiritual food and spiritual drink and eternal life, through your servant Jesus.

**4** Above all, we thank you: you are powerful. Glory be to you forever.

**5** Lord, remember your Church — rescue it from every evil, bring it to wholeness in your love, and gather it in from the four winds — holy and complete — into the kingdom you have made ready for it. Yours is the power and the glory, forever.

**6** Let grace come. Let this world pass away.
Hosanna to the God of David.
If you are holy — come.
If you are not — repent.
**Maranatha!** [Our Lord, come!]
Amen.

**7** As for the prophets — let them give thanks as the Spirit moves them.

---

*PNEUMA note: This post-communion prayer is breathtaking. It moves from gratitude (vv. 2-4) to intercession (v. 5) to a stunning eschatological cry (v. 6). "Maranatha!" — preserved in the original Aramaic even in this Greek text — is the oldest Christian prayer we possess: two Aramaic words shouted by Jesus's own disciples, still ringing across twenty centuries. "Let this world pass away" is not despair but longing — a community living at the edge of two ages. And then: "If you are holy — come." The table is open, but it demands holiness.*
